answer: src/urllib3/util/url.py was changed for several reasons across its history: to implement RFC 3986 URL parsing to align with the Python standard library, to percent-encode invalid characters (such as '@' symbols in email usernames) within the auth section for proxy users, and to make regular expressions private to protect internal APIs.

citations.author: sethmlarson
citations.quote: This brings our URL parser in-line with Python standard library parsing which all use RFC 3986.

citations.author: sethmlarson
citations.quote:
Make all `urllib3.util.url` regular expressions private to protect our internal APIs
- Change `Url` to a `typing.NamedTuple`
- Removed `get_host` and `split_first` deprecated APIs
- `idna` doesn't have type hints *yet*!

citations.author: sethmlarson
citations.quote: Mostly proxy users that have their email address as their "username" and therefore have an `@` symbol within the auth section.

decisions.rationale: Proxy users had their email address as their username containing an @ symbol, causing issues across both the library and requests issue trackers.
decisions.summary: Percent-encode invalid characters within auth section and remove rfc3986 as a vendored dependency

decisions.rationale: This brings our URL parser in-line with Python standard library parsing which all use RFC 3986.
decisions.summary: Implement RFC 3986 URL parsing by adding the rfc3986 module
